title: Shiprocket IPO Subscribed 99 Times as Allotment Nears, GMP Points to Strong Listing
excerpt: The e-commerce logistics platform's ₹1,617 crore IPO drew massive oversubscription across all investor categories, with grey market premiums suggesting a 24-31% listing gain when shares debut on August 19.
body:
• Shiprocket's ₹1,617.48 crore IPO was subscribed 99.38 times overall, with institutional investors bidding 122.80x their reserved portion.
  • The grey market premium has fluctuated between ₹14 and ₹31, suggesting a listing price of ₹111-128 against the upper band price of ₹97.
  • Allotment is expected on August 17, with shares scheduled to list on BSE and NSE on August 19.
  • The company turned EBITDA-positive in FY26, reporting ₹2,024 crore in revenue and ₹53 crore in operating cash flow, though it posted a net loss of ₹79.2 crore.

Massive Oversubscription Across Categories

Shiprocket's initial public offering closed on August 14 with total subscriptions reaching 99.38 times the shares on offer, reflecting strong demand for the Temasek-backed e-commerce enablement platform.

Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIBs) led the charge, subscribing 122.80 times their reserved portion. Non-institutional investors (HNIs) bid 88.64 times, while retail individual investors subscribed 45.00 times. The employee reserved category saw the strongest relative demand at 54.43 times.

The company had already raised ₹727.41 crore from anchor investors ahead of the public offering, allotting 7.50 crore shares at ₹97 apiece, with mutual funds accounting for a significant share of the allocation.

IPO Structure and Pricing

The book-built issue was priced at ₹92-97 per share, with the total size of ₹1,617.48 crore comprising a fresh issue of ₹885.50 crore and an Offer for Sale (OFS) of ₹731.98 crore. Existing shareholders selling through the OFS include Lightrock, Tribe Capital, Moore Strategic Ventures, Agility International Investment, and co-founders Gautam Kapoor, Saahil Goel, and Vishesh Khurana.

Shiprocket trimmed the IPO size from the ₹2,342 crore proposed in its updated draft prospectus filed in December 2025. CEO Saahil Goel attributed the reduction to stronger profitability and cash generation, noting the company generated ₹53 crore in operating cash flow during FY26.

"The business generated ₹53 crore of cash flow in FY26 while substantially improving its financial position."

— Saahil Goel, Co-founder and CEO, Shiprocket

GMP Signals Listing Gains

In the grey market, Shiprocket shares have been trading at premiums ranging from ₹14 to ₹31 over the issue price. At the higher end, this implies a listing price of approximately ₹128, representing a 31% gain over the upper band price of ₹97.

At the upper price band, the IPO implies a post-issue market capitalization of approximately ₹7,058 crore — a significant markdown from its peak private valuation of ₹10,000 crore set during a December 2024 funding round from Koch Group, MUFG, and Huddle Ventures.

Brokerages have maintained a largely positive view of the issue, citing Shiprocket's expanding merchant base, asset-light business model, and exposure to India's growing e-commerce market.

Business Fundamentals

Founded in 2011, Shiprocket is India's largest new-age horizontal e-commerce enablement platform by revenue, according to a Redseer report. The company serves over 145,000 active merchants across 146 countries, processing more than 97 million transactions.

Its core business focuses on shipping aggregation and order fulfillment for MSMEs and D2C brands, providing access to multiple logistics partners through a single technology platform. The emerging business segment extends into cargo, cross-border shipping, advertising, marketing tools, and a checkout platform.

Revenue rose 24% to ₹2,024 crore in FY26 from ₹1,632 crore the previous year. While the net loss held flat at ₹79.2 crore due to non-cash expenses, the company turned EBITDA-positive and generated positive operating cash flow for the first time.

Timeline and What to Watch

The basis of allotment is expected to be finalized on August 17, with refunds and share credits scheduled for August 18. Listing on BSE and NSE is tentatively set for August 19.

Investors who applied can check allotment status through the registrar KFin Technologies' website or via their brokerage platforms. With the IPO priced conservatively relative to the company's last private round, the listing day performance will test whether public markets are ready to reward profitability-bound logistics-tech platforms.
author: Diaspora Desk
